content.value_statement: Vue 2 and Webpack 4 projects can require different setup choices than modern Vite applications. This skill provides focused integration guidance for styles, workers, streaming, and safe rendering settings.
actual_capabilities: Identifies when a project uses Vue 2 with Vue CLI or Webpack 4-era tooling.
Recommends installing markstream-vue2 and only required peer dependencies.
Explains where to import the package stylesheet.
Recommends CDN worker factories for Mermaid and KaTeX when workers are required.
Provides smooth-streaming, fade, and typewriter defaults for chat interfaces.
Explains safe HTML policy and Mermaid strict-mode defaults.
limitations: It targets Vue 2, Vue CLI, and Webpack 4-style projects, not Vite-first applications.
It does not install packages, modify files, or run build commands by itself.
CDN worker availability and content security policies require project-specific verification.
Trusted HTML rendering requires a separate security review of the content source.

use_cases.title: Add Markdown rendering to a legacy app
use_cases.description: Set up markstream-vue2 styles and compatible rendering defaults in a Vue CLI application.

use_cases.title: Build a streaming chat view
use_cases.description: Configure content streaming, fade behavior, and cursor behavior for an AI chat interface.

use_cases.title: Migrate a Webpack 4 renderer
use_cases.description: Replace fragile worker or Monaco setup choices with compatible Mermaid, KaTeX, and code-block guidance.

prompt_templates.title: Start a Vue 2 integration
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me add markstream-vue2 to my Vue 2 Vue CLI project. List the required installation and stylesheet steps.

prompt_templates.title: Configure Mermaid and KaTeX
prompt_templates.prompt: My Vue 2 Webpack 4 app needs Mermaid and KaTeX. Recommend a worker setup that avoids Vite-specific imports.

prompt_templates.title: Create a streaming chat renderer
prompt_templates.prompt: Configure MarkdownRender for a Vue 2 chat UI that streams new content and later displays completed history.

prompt_templates.title: Review trusted rendering exception
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this Vue 2 rendering surface. Explain when html-policy trusted and Mermaid strict mode disabled are appropriate, and list safeguards.

output_examples.input: Set up markstream-vue2 in a Vue CLI app.
output: Install markstream-vue2 with only the needed peers.
Import the package stylesheet from the application shell.
Use content for ordinary chat streaming.
Use automatic smooth streaming while content arrives.
Disable fade during streaming to avoid flicker.
Switch to completed-history settings when final is true.
Keep the safe HTML policy by default.
Limit trusted mode to the reviewed legacy surface.
Document why the exception is necessary.

best_practices: Confirm the project uses Vue 2 and Webpack 4-style tooling before applying the guidance.
Keep safe HTML policy and Mermaid strict mode unless a reviewed trusted surface requires an exception.
Validate the smallest useful local build or development command after integration.
anti_patterns: Do not use Vite-specific worker imports in a Webpack 4 project.
Do not add Monaco worker wiring when stable code block rendering meets the requirement.
Do not enable trusted HTML rendering for unreviewed or user-controlled content.

faq.question: Who should use this skill?
faq.answer: Use it for Vue 2 applications built with Vue CLI or similar Webpack 4-era tooling.

faq.question: Does it support Vite projects?
faq.answer: No. It specifically warns against Vite-style worker imports for this target stack.

faq.question: Where should the stylesheet be imported?
faq.answer: Import the markstream-vue2 distribution stylesheet in the application shell.

faq.question: How should Mermaid and KaTeX workers be configured?
faq.answer: Use the package CDN worker factories when workers are needed, then verify your security policy allows them.

faq.question: What is the recommended default for HTML?
faq.answer: Keep the safe HTML policy unless a reviewed trusted legacy surface needs a narrow exception.

faq.question: Does the skill run commands automatically?
faq.answer: No. It provides integration guidance and recommends validating with a suitable local command.
